question_text: The rate at which a tree grows $t$ years after planting is given by $G(t) = \frac{2.5}{t + 1}\text{ metres per year}$.

subparts.stem: Explain why the tree is always growing taller.
subparts.final_answer: $The tree is always growing taller because $G(t) > 0$ for all $t \ge 0$.$

mark_breakdown.desc: Concluding that the rate of growth is positive so the tree is always growing taller

subparts.solution:
$G(t) > 0$ for all $t \ge 0$.
$\therefore$ the rate at which the tree grows is always positive.
$\therefore$ the tree is always growing taller.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: If the rate of change of a quantity is strictly positive, the quantity is strictly increasing.
step_by_step: Conclude that growth rate is strictly positive, meaning the tree is always growing.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Confusing the rate of growth being positive with the rate being increasing or decreasing.

subparts.stem: Evaluate the following integrals, and interpret their meaning: $\int_0^5 G(t)\,\text{d}t$

mark_breakdown.desc: Substituting limits 0 to 5 to obtain $2.5\ln 6 \approx 4.48\text{ metres}$

subparts.solution:
$$\int_0^5 G(t)\,dt = \int_0^5 \frac{2.5}{t+1}\,dt$$
$$= [2.5\ln|t+1|]_0^5$$
$$= 2.5\ln 6 - 2.5\ln 1$$
$$= 2.5\ln 6 \approx 4.48\text{ metres}$$

The tree grew about $4.48\text{ metres}$ in the first 5 years of its lifetime.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The total change in height is the integral of the rate of growth with respect to time: $\Delta h = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} G(t)\,dt$.
step_by_step: Use $\ln 1 = 0$ to simplify to $2.5\ln 6$ and calculate the numerical value.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting that $\ln(1) = 0$ or forgetting the factor of $2.5$.

subparts.stem: Evaluate the following integrals, and interpret their meaning: $\int_5^{10} G(t)\,\text{d}t$

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up the integral from 5 to 10

subparts.solution:
$$\int_5^{10} G(t)\,dt = \int_5^{10} \frac{2.5}{t+1}\,dt$$
$$= [2.5\ln|t+1|]_5^{10}$$
$$= 2.5\ln 11 - 2.5\ln 6$$
$$= 2.5\ln\left(\frac{11}{6}\right) \approx 1.52\text{ metres}$$

The tree grew about $1.52\text{ metres}$ between the 5th and 10th years of its lifetime.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The net growth between two time periods $t=a$ and $t=b$ is given by $\int_a^b G(t)\,dt$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using limits 0 to 10 instead of 5 to 10.

subparts.stem: After 15 years, the tree is struck by lightning and is cut down. How much did the tree grow over its lifetime?
subparts.solution:
$$\int_0^{15} G(t)\,dt = \int_0^{15} \frac{2.5}{t+1}\,dt$$
$$= [2.5\ln|t+1|]_0^{15}$$
$$= 2.5\ln 16 - 2.5\ln 1$$
$$= 2.5\ln 16 \approx 6.93\text{ metres}$$

The tree grew about $6.93\text{ metres}$ over its entire lifetime.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The total lifetime growth is the definite integral of the growth rate over the entire lifetime interval $[0, 15]$.
step_by_step: Set limits of integration from 0 to 15.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Plugging in incorrect upper or lower limits.
